senses.en: a large heavy animal of the cow family, used in Asia for pulling ploughs and carts
examples: A **buffalo** was standing in the middle of the paddy field.
My grandfather still uses a **buffalo** to plough the rice fields.
The boys rode the **buffalo** home along the river path.

buffalo.note: In Viet Nam this almost always means the **water buffalo**. The plural can be *buffalo* (unchanged) or *buffaloes* — both are correct.

senses.en: a field filled with shallow water where rice is grown
senses.vi: ruộng lúa nước, cánh đồng lúa
examples: The **paddy fields** turn bright green in early summer.
We walked along the narrow path between two **paddy fields**.
Her parents work in the **paddy fields** from dawn.

paddy field.note: Also written *rice paddy* or just *paddy*. *Paddy* on its own can also mean rice that still has its husk on.

senses.en: the time when crops are gathered from the fields, or the crops that are gathered
examples: The rice **harvest** begins in October.
It was a good **harvest** this year — the best for a decade.
The whole village helps at **harvest** time.

senses.en: to gather a crop from the fields
examples: They **harvest** the rice twice a year.
The corn is **harvested** in late August.

senses.en: a piece of land where fruit trees are grown
examples: My uncle has an **orchard** behind his house.
We picked apples in the **orchard** all morning.
The **orchard** is full of mango trees.

orchard.note: An **orchard** is for fruit *trees*. A *garden* is a general word, and a *vegetable garden* grows vegetables instead.

senses.en: cows and bulls kept on a farm for their milk or meat
examples: The **cattle** are grazing in the field.
His family keeps about forty **cattle**.
We drove the **cattle** down to the stream to drink.

cattle.note: **Always plural** — *the cattle **are** in the field*, never *is*. There is no form *a cattle* or *cattles*; for one animal say *a cow* or *a bull*.

senses.en: a large group of animals of the same kind that live or are kept together
examples: A **herd** of buffalo crossed the road in front of us.
The farmer has a **herd** of thirty cows.
We watched a **herd** of elephants at the waterhole.

senses.en: to move animals, or people, together as a group
examples: The boy **herded** the goats back to the barn.
We were **herded** onto the bus like sheep.

herd.note: Use **herd** for cows, buffalo and elephants; *flock* for birds and sheep; *school* for fish. Sounds exactly like *heard*.

senses.en: a large farm building used for storing crops or keeping animals in
senses.vi: nhà kho, chuồng gia súc (ở trang trại)
examples: The hay is kept in the **barn**.
We shelter the cattle in the **barn** in winter.
There is an old wooden **barn** behind the farmhouse.

senses.en: a deep hole dug in the ground to reach water
examples: Every morning she draws water from the **well**.
The village **well** dried up during the drought.
There is an old stone **well** in the yard.

senses.en: in a good or satisfactory way
examples: She sings very **well**.
He didn't sleep **well** last night.

well.note: In this unit it is the **noun** — a hole for water. Do not confuse the adverb *well* (*she plays well*) with the adjective *good* (*she is a good player*).

senses.en: a small narrow river
examples: The children were playing in the **stream**.
A small **stream** runs behind our house.
We crossed the **stream** on stepping stones.

senses.en: to send or receive video or music over the internet as it plays
examples: We **streamed** the match on my phone.
The concert was **streamed** live.

stream.note: Size order: a **stream** is smaller than a *river*; a *brook* is smaller still.

senses.en: a tall tropical plant with hard hollow stems, used for building and for making furniture
examples: The fence is made of **bamboo**.
**Bamboo** grows very quickly — up to a metre a day.
She was carrying two baskets on a **bamboo** pole.

bamboo.note: Usually uncountable when you mean the material: *made of bamboo*. Stress the second syllable: bam-**BOO**.

senses.en: extremely large in area or amount
examples: A **vast** paddy field stretched to the mountains.
The country has **vast** areas of forest.
There is a **vast** difference between the two villages.

forms.en: very much; to a great degree
forms.ex: Life here is **vastly** different from the city.

vast.note: Stronger than *big* or *large*, and used for open space or quantity — not usually for a single object. Rhymes with *fast*.

senses.en: quiet and calm, without noise or worry
examples: The countryside is much more **peaceful** than the city.
We spent a **peaceful** afternoon by the stream.
It is so **peaceful** here in the early morning.

senses.en: not involving war, violence or argument
examples: They found a **peaceful** solution to the dispute.
It was a **peaceful** protest.

forms.en: a situation with no war, or a state of calm
forms.ex: I just want a bit of **peace** and quiet.

senses.en: to put a large quantity of things onto a vehicle or into a container
examples: They **loaded** the rice onto the cart.
Help me **load** the truck before it rains.
The buffalo cart was **loaded** with bamboo.

senses.en: something heavy that is being carried
examples: He carried a heavy **load** of firewood.
That's the third **load** of hay today.

load.note: Opposite: **unload**. Note the pair *load the cart* (the cart is the object) and *load the rice onto the cart* (the rice is).

senses.en: to take fruit off a tree or plant by hand
examples: In summer we **pick fruit** in my uncle's orchard.
The children love to **pick fruit** straight from the tree.
We spent the morning **picking fruit** and the afternoon swimming.

pick fruit.note: **Pick** here means take *off* the plant. *Pick up* is different — it means lift something from the ground.

senses.en: to gather eggs from where hens have laid them
examples: Every morning I **collect eggs** from the hen house.
It's my job to **collect the eggs** before school.
She **collected** six **eggs** today.
colloc: collect eggs from the hen house

senses.en: to sit on a horse and control it as it moves
examples: My cousin can **ride a horse** very well.
I learned to **ride a horse** when I was eight.
They **rode horses** along the beach at sunset.

ride a horse.note: Irregular: ride → **rode** → **ridden**. Use *ride* for horses, bikes and motorbikes; use *drive* for cars.

senses.en: to make a kite rise and stay in the air on the end of a string
examples: On windy afternoons we **fly kites** on the hill.
He taught his little sister to **fly a kite**.
It's too still today — you can't **fly a kite** without wind.
colloc: fly a kite in the wind

senses.en: a member of a group of people who move from place to place instead of living in one
examples: The **nomads** move their herds to new grass each season.
For centuries **nomads** have crossed these plains.
His grandparents were **nomads** before they settled in the village.

forms.en: moving from place to place rather than living in one
forms.vi: du mục, nay đây mai đó

senses.en: friendly and generous towards guests and visitors
examples: The people here are so **hospitable** that a stranger is offered tea within a minute.
Her family was **hospitable** to us for a whole week.
Everyone had told me the village was **hospitable**, and it was.

senses.en: (of a place or weather) pleasant enough to live in or travel through
senses.vi: dễ chịu, thuận lợi (nơi chốn, thời tiết)
examples: The valley is far more **hospitable** in spring than in December.
Few plants grow there; it is not a **hospitable** place.

hospitable.note: Nothing to do with a **hospital**. The stress is on the second syllable: *hos-**PI**-ta-ble*. Opposite: **inhospitable**.

senses.en: pretty to look at, especially in an old-fashioned way
senses.vi: đẹp như tranh (phong cảnh, làng mạc)
examples: Wooden houses stand along the water in the most **picturesque** part of the village.
We stopped to photograph a **picturesque** stone bridge.
The road to the coast is slow, but it is **picturesque**.

picturesque.note: Used for places, buildings and views — not for people. Stress the **last** syllable, which rhymes with *desk*: /ˌpɪktʃəˈresk/.

senses.en: having had a lot of good training, and so able to do a job properly
senses.vi: lành nghề, được đào tạo tốt
examples: A **well-trained** buffalo will stop at one word.
The farm needs **well-trained** workers who can drive the machines.
Their dog is **well-trained** — it never goes near the chickens.

forms.en: the process of learning the skills for a job
forms.vi: sự đào tạo, sự huấn luyện

well-trained.note: Keep the hyphen before a noun: *a **well-trained** dog*. Opposites: *badly trained*, *untrained*.

senses.en: with something on every side
examples: The house is **surrounded by** green trees.
Their village is **surrounded** by water on three sides.
We ate in a small yard **surrounded** by flowers.

senses.en: to be all round something
examples: A low brick wall **surrounds** the temple.
Paddy fields **surround** the village on every side.

forms.en: everything around a place or a person

surrounded (by).note: The partner word is **by**: *surrounded **by** trees*, never ❌ *surrounded around trees*.

senses.en: the hills, fields, water and trees you can see in a country area, especially when they are beautiful
examples: The train slows down where the **scenery** is best.
Nobody spoke for ten minutes; we just looked at the **scenery**.
I miss the **scenery** more than anything else about my grandparents' village.

forms.ex: We took the **scenic** road along the river.

scenery.note: **Uncountable** — never ❌ *sceneries* and never ❌ *a scenery*. Say *beautiful **scenery***. A **scene** is one single view or one part of a film; **scenery** is the whole countryside you can see.

senses.en: a large farm machine that cuts a crop and separates the grain from the stalks in one operation
examples: Two **combine harvesters** finished the whole field before lunch.
Before the **combine harvester** arrived, the village cut the rice by hand.
A **combine harvester** does in an hour what once took my grandfather a day.
colloc: harvest rice with a combine harvester

combine harvester.note: Often shortened to just **combine**. The first word is stressed on its first syllable here — /ˈkɒmbaɪn/ — unlike the verb *to combine* /kəmˈbaɪn/.

senses.en: to break up and turn over soil so that seeds can be planted
examples: The farmers **plough** the fields before the rains come.
He **ploughed** four hectares with one buffalo.
This heavy soil is easier to **plough** after a wet night.

senses.en: a farm tool with a curved blade, pulled by an animal or a tractor, that turns over soil
examples: An old wooden **plough** hangs on the barn wall.
The buffalo pulled the **plough** slowly to the end of the row.

plough.note: British spelling **plough**, American spelling **plow** — both are accepted. It rhymes with *now*, not with *though*.

senses.en: to prepare land and grow crops on it
examples: The land beside the river has been **cultivated** for hundreds of years.
They **cultivate** rice on the flat ground and tea on the slopes.
Only a narrow strip of the valley can be **cultivated**.

senses.en: to develop a habit, a skill or a friendship slowly and on purpose
senses.vi: rèn luyện, gây dựng (thói quen, quan hệ)
examples: He **cultivated** the habit of reading half an hour before bed.
She has **cultivated** a friendship with everyone on the lane.

forms.en: the growing of crops on land
forms.vi: sự trồng trọt, sự canh tác
forms.ex: Rice **cultivation** here goes back a thousand years.

cultivate.note: More formal than *grow*. You **cultivate** land or a crop; you **grow** a plant.

senses.en: a plant such as rice, maize or coffee that farmers grow in large amounts
examples: Coffee is the most important **crop** in the highlands.
This village grows two **crops** of rice a year.
A week of heavy rain damaged the **crops**.

senses.en: the amount of a plant that is gathered in one season
senses.vi: vụ mùa, sản lượng thu hoạch
examples: Last year's rice **crop** was the best for a decade.
A cold spring ruined the fruit **crop**.

crop.note: Countable: *one crop, two **crops***. The **crops** are what stands in the field; the **harvest** is the gathering of them.

senses.en: birds such as chickens, ducks and geese that are kept on a farm for their eggs or meat
examples: The family sells eggs and **poultry** at the Sunday market.
The **poultry** are shut in at night because of the foxes.
He keeps cattle at one end of the farm and **poultry** at the other.

senses.en: the meat of these birds, as food
examples: The recipe works with **poultry** or with pork.
She eats no red meat, only fish and **poultry**.

poultry.note: Uncountable — never ❌ *a poultry* or ❌ *poultries*. When it means the live birds it takes a plural verb: *The **poultry are** fed at six.*

senses.en: to take fish out of water with a net, a line or a trap
examples: Some families here live by **catching fish** in the canals.
We **caught** six small **fish** before breakfast.
You can **catch fish** in the pond behind the temple.

catch fish.note: Irregular: catch → **caught** → **caught**. The plural of *fish* is usually **fish**: *three **fish***, not ❌ *three fishes*. **Catch fish** is the action; **fishing** is the activity — *go **fishing***.

senses.en: to take milk from a cow, a buffalo or a goat
examples: She **milks** the cows at five every morning.
My cousin showed me how to **milk** a goat.
The buffalo has already been **milked** today.

senses.en: the white liquid that cows and other animals produce as food for their young
examples: We carried the fresh **milk** home in a metal can.
Buffalo **milk** is thicker than cow's **milk**.

milk (a cow).note: As a verb the animal is the object: ***milk** the cow*. Say *get milk **from** a cow* only when you mean the liquid, not the job.

senses.en: to make something lose the water in it, usually by leaving it in the sun or the air
examples: After the harvest they **dry** the rice on the road in front of the houses.
We **dried** the chillies on a mat in the yard.
Fish is **dried** in the sun and then kept for months.

senses.en: with no water in it or on it
examples: The path is **dry** enough to cycle on now.
Keep the seed somewhere **dry** until spring.

dry (rice).note: Verb forms: dry → **dried** → **dried**; *he **dries***. Keep the verb and the adjective apart: *They **dry** the rice* (an action) / *The rice is **dry*** (a state).

senses.en: to take goods off a vehicle, a boat or an animal
examples: It took the three of us an hour to **unload** the rice.
The truck was **unloaded** in the yard behind the barn.
Wait until the boat has been **unloaded** before you get on.
colloc: unload the rice from a cart

unload.note: The opposite of **load**. Two patterns: ***unload** the truck* (the vehicle) and ***unload** the rice **from** the truck* (the goods).

senses.en: a narrow passage of water dug by people, either for boats or to carry water to fields
examples: The **canal** is just deep enough for a small boat.
Boys were swimming in the **canal** beside the road.
Every field on this side is fed by a **canal**.

canal.note: Stress the **second** syllable: *ca-**NAL*** /kəˈnæl/. A **canal** is made by people; a natural one is a **stream** or a **river**.

senses.en: a boat that carries people, cars or goods across water on a regular route
examples: The **ferry** to the island leaves every two hours.
We pushed the motorbikes onto the **ferry** and crossed the river.
There was a **ferry** here before they built the bridge.

senses.en: to carry people or things a short distance, again and again
examples: A small boat **ferries** visitors across the canal all day.
Her father **ferried** the whole team to the match.

ferry.note: *Travel **by ferry*** has no *the*, but *take **the** ferry* does. Plural: **ferries**.

senses.en: a tall tower by the sea with a strong light at the top that warns ships away from danger
examples: A white **lighthouse** stands at the far end of the beach.
The **lighthouse** has kept ships off these rocks for a century.
You can climb to the top of the **lighthouse** and see the whole island.

lighthouse.note: One word, no space. The *gh* is silent: /ˈlaɪthaʊs/.

senses.en: a food or product that a place is famous for making well
examples: Every village along this road has its own **speciality**.
Green bean cake is the **speciality** of my grandmother's town.
Visitors buy the local **specialities** to take home to their families.

senses.en: a subject or a skill that somebody knows a great deal about
examples: Vietnamese history is his **speciality**.
Mending old bicycles is my uncle's **speciality**.

speciality.note: British English **speciality** /ˌspeʃiˈæləti/; American English **specialty** /ˈspeʃəlti/ — both are accepted. Plural: **specialities**.
